problems.title: A shared absolute-value factor
problems.question: Solve |x²-2x|<|x-2|.
problems.idea: Factor the left side and handle the zero shared factor.
steps: The inequality is |x|·|x-2|<|x-2|.
At x=2 it reads 0<0 and fails. For x≠2, divide by the positive |x-2| to get |x|<1.
This gives -1<x<1, already excluding 2.

problems.title: Use sum and product in a symmetric system
problems.question: Solve a²-ab+b²=7, a+b+ab=11 over the reals.
steps: The second equation gives P=11-S. Substitution into the first gives S²+3S-40=0=(S-5)(S+8).
If S=5, then P=6, so a,b are the roots of t²-5t+6=0: 2 and 3.
If S=-8, then P=19. The quadratic t²+8t+19 has discriminant 64-76<0, so it gives no real a,b.

problems.title: Split a quadratic system into two lines
problems.question: Solve x²+2xy-3y²=0 and x²+x+y²-2y=1.
problems.idea: Factor the first equation and substitute each linear case.
steps: If x=y, the second equation becomes 2y²-y-1=(2y+1)(y-1)=0, giving (1,1) and (-1/2,-1/2).
If x=-3y, it becomes 10y²-5y-1=0.
Thus y=(5±√65)/20 and x=-3y.
The zero-product split covers every solution.

problems.title: A cube-sum condition on two parameter roots
problems.question: For which a do the two roots x₁,x₂ of x²-(a+2)x+a+1=0 satisfy x₁³+x₂³>0?
problems.idea: Factor the quadratic and use monotonicity of the cube.
steps: The roots are 1 and a+1.
Their cube sum is 1+(a+1)³. It is positive exactly when (a+1)³>-1.
Cubing is strictly increasing, so a+1>-1, giving a>-2.
problems.answer: a>-2; if two distinct roots are required, also exclude a=0.
problems.note: The statement does not explicitly say “distinct.” At a=0 the roots coincide at 1 and still satisfy the positive cube-sum condition when roots are counted with multiplicity.

problems.title: An isosceles triangle from a median to a leg
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base 6 cm and median 7.5 cm to an equal side. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the median formula to find the equal side, then the altitude.
steps: Let the equal side be s. The median to it satisfies 7.5²=(2·6²+s²)/4.
The altitude to the base is √(153-3²)=12.
The area is 6·12/2=36.

problems.title: Four triangles made by intersecting diagonals
problems.question: A convex quadrilateral’s diagonals divide it into four triangles. Two have equal areas; the other two have areas 5 and 10 cm². Find the total area.
problems.idea: Products of opposite small-triangle areas are equal.
formulas: For four triangles around the same crossing, opposite-area products are equal because they use the same four diagonal pieces and the same sine factor.
steps: The two equal areas must be opposite. If they were adjacent, the other two would also have to be equal, contrary to 5 and 10.
Let each equal area be t. Then t²=5·10=50, so t=5√2.
The total is 5+10+2t=15+10√2.

problems.title: Area between a base and the diagonal midpoints
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD with BC∥AD, diagonals meet at K. Areas BKC=9 and AKD=25. M,N are the midpoints of AC,BD. Find area AMND.
problems.idea: The square roots of those small areas give the base ratio.
formulas: Base ratio=√(opposite triangle area ratio); total trapezoid area=(√S₁+√S₂)²; diagonal-midpoint segment=half the base difference.
steps: The base ratio BC:AD=3:5. Write the bases as 3t and 5t.
The whole area is (3+5)²=64, so with height h, 4th=64 and th=16.
MN is parallel to the bases, halfway up, with length (5t-3t)/2=t.
AMND has height h/2 and bases 5t,t. Its area is (5t+t)(h/2)/2=3th/2=24.

problems.title: Digits constrained by two division remainders
problems.question: A two-digit number divided by its digit sum gives quotient 4, remainder 3; divided by its digit product gives quotient 3, remainder 5. Find it.
problems.idea: Use tens digit t and units digit u.
steps: The first condition is 10t+u=4(t+u)+3, giving u=2t-1.
The second is 10t+u=3tu+5. Substitute u to get 2t²-5t+2=0=(2t-1)(t-2).
Only t=2 is an integer digit; then u=3 and the number is 23.
Check: 23=4·5+3=3·6+5, with valid remainders.

problems.title: Small triangle between three bisectors in a rectangle
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, AB=6,BC=8. B- and D-bisectors meet A-bisector AE at K,T. The D-bisector meets BC at F, and AE meets BC at E. Find area FTE.
problems.idea: Use coordinates and the 45° angle bisectors.
steps: Set A=(0,0),B=(0,6),C=(8,6),D=(8,0). The A-bisector is y=x, so E=(6,6).
The D-bisector is y=8-x, giving F=(2,6) and T=(4,4).
FE=4 and T is 2 below line FE.
The area is 4·2/2=4.

problems.title: Maximize an inscribed rectangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 5 cm and base 6 cm. A rectangle has two vertices on the base and the others on the equal sides. Find its greatest area.
problems.idea: Express the rectangle’s width through its height using similarity.
formulas: Triangle height=√(5²-3²)=4; width at height y=6(1-y/4).
steps: For 0≤y≤4, the area is A(y)=6y-(3/2)y².
Complete the square: A(y)=6-(3/2)(y-2)².
The maximum is 6, attained at height 2 and width 3.
